measured.note:
Julia shares no ancestry with the managed-OO family, and the lane was built in the opposite order from every other one here: the GRAMMAR WAS MEASURED FIRST. `script/m60/julia-census.ts` ran before an analyzer existed, because every lane in this repo was written first and measured afterwards and the measurement is what finds the defects — objective-c was closed over an instrument reading 7 of 329 files whose '0 grammar errors' was 49 crashes counted as clean parses. Four constructs were then patched in the grammar itself (185 -> 177 error files) and the analyzer written against the patched result.

The grammar is almost entirely POSITIONAL: 7 of 151 named node types carry field names, so everything else must be navigated by child ORDER. `scoped_identifier` does not exist in this grammar (0 occurrences in 400 files — qualified access is a nested `field_expression`); `binary_expression`'s operator is a NAMED child at index 1, so `pos(node,1)` is the operator and not the right operand; a `where` clause wraps the callable in a `where_expression`, whose BARE form puts the type variable there as a sibling identifier, so scanning for a name returns the parameter. Each of those produced a plausible wrong answer on files that parse with zero ERROR nodes.

Qualified names are kept WHOLE: measured over 400 files, 1,352 bare segments appear behind a qualified path and 72 are reachable by MORE THAN ONE distinct path (`parse` is `Meta.parse`/`Base.parse`/`TOML.parse`/`Dates.parse`), so collapsing to the last segment fuses unrelated functions into one node.

The lane's own fixture caught 3 defects AND 2 errors in the expectations, and the mutant set caught 3 mutants that were inert no-ops plus 2 genuine fixture gaps — the fixture was silent rather than correct. `expectSymbols` matches name AND kind, so an extra wrongly-kinded symbol beside a correct one passes unnoticed.

Performance was the first measurement nobody had taken, and it found a defect every correctness number walked past: `complexity()` is a full tree walk called ONCE PER SYMBOL, giving every symbol the FILE's complexity. `test/core.jl` took 228 s alone; the 941-file corpus took 969 s. Now 728 ms and 172 s. The residual is not the analyzer — the worst remaining file spends 16.7 s inside tree-sitter's own `parse()` and 124 ms here.

WHAT THE ORACLES FOUND, since that is the argument for them rather than the row's arithmetic. Each was a defect the fixtures and the mutants both missed: a construction BEFORE its type declaration was a plain call (a comment claimed the opposite of what the code did); a field read published the RECEIVER instead of the member, inverting every `uses` row for every field access in the language; a qualified type annotation named the MODULE; a parameterised type in a namespace had no reference at all; a `where {T<:Real}` bound was invisible because the braced spelling hides it in a curly_expression; a macro's expansion-local binding was published as a member of the macro. Six independently derived implementations, six defects, none of which any count would have shown — each edge was present, plausible, and named a real identifier in the file.

The discipline that produced them: expectations authored from Julia semantics BEFORE the analyzer ran, and mutants written as faithful reverts of defects actually shipped. That pairing caught 2 errors in the fixtures themselves, 3 mutants that were inert no-ops returning the result unchanged, and 2 mutants that survived because the fixture and the analyzer were agreeing on NOTHING.
